title: Biclosed matrix convolution structure
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, and let $\mathbf V=\operatorname{Ch}(R)$ carry the projective closed monoidal structure of [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model]. For a small set $S$, let $\mathbf G_S$ be the graph category with coordinatewise model structure of [lem-coef-graph-product-model]. Define $(P\star Q)(s,t)=\bigoplus_{u\in S}P(u,t)\otimes Q(s,u)$ and $E(s,t)=R[0]$ for $s=t$ and $0$ otherwise. Then $\star$ is an associative unital biclosed monoidal product (not assumed symmetric). The functor $P\star-$ is left adjoint to $R_P$, and $-\star Q$ is left adjoint to $L_Q$, with products of internal Hom complexes given by $R_P(H)(s,u)=\prod_t\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P(u,t),H(s,t))$ and $L_Q(H)(u,t)=\prod_s\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(Q(s,u),H(s,t))$.

source.place: Muro Definition 10.1, pp. 1595-1596 (PDF pages 55-56): matrix tensor, diagonal unit, and the two internal-Hom adjoints, specialized to the closed symmetric monoidal category of complexes.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model] and [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model], the underlying category $\mathbf V$ is closed symmetric monoidal, with unit $I=R[0]$, direct-sum total tensor, and product total internal Hom, denoted $[A,C]$. Thus closedness and symmetry give natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf V}(A\otimes B,C)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf V}(B,[A,C])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf V}(A,[B,C])$, where the second identification includes interchanging $A$ and $B$. By [lem-coef-graph-product-model], $\mathbf G_S=\prod_{S^2}\mathbf V$ is complete and cocomplete. Products and coproducts of complexes can be formed degreewise with coordinatewise differential; their projection and inclusion maps satisfy the respective universal properties also for chain maps. A graph morphism is an arbitrary family of chain maps, so its Hom set is the product of the coordinate Hom sets. Smallness of $S$ ensures that all the indicated sums and products exist.

source.place: Definition 10.1, printed pp. 1595-1596; ambient hypotheses in Notation, printed p. 1545. Existing nodes supply the category of complexes.

proof.text: Tensor distributes over every small coproduct in either variable, including the empty one. Indeed, closedness from [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model] gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf V}(A\otimes\bigoplus_iB_i,C)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf V}(\bigoplus_iB_i,[A,C])\cong\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf V}(A\otimes B_i,C)$. These bijections are restriction along $A\otimes B_i\to A\otimes\bigoplus_iB_i$, so these maps exhibit a coproduct. Symmetry gives the other variable, and the empty case gives $A\otimes0\cong0\cong0\otimes A$. For graph maps $f:P\to P\prime$ and $g:Q\to Q\prime$, define $f\star g$ on the $u$-summand by $f(u,t)\otimes g(s,u)$ followed by its target inclusion. The tensor bifunctor laws and the coproduct universal property give the identity and composition laws. This constructs the stated bifunctor.

source.place: Definition 10.1: elementary universal-property construction of the matrix tensor on maps and its distributivity identifications.

proof.text: At $(s,t)$, expand the two triple products using Step 2. The source $((P\star Q)\star T)(s,t)$ is the coproduct over $(u,v)\in S^2$ of $(P(v,t)\otimes Q(u,v))\otimes T(s,u)$, while $(P\star(Q\star T))(s,t)$ is the coproduct over the same pairs of $P(v,t)\otimes(Q(u,v)\otimes T(s,u))$. Define the associator on each summand by the tensor associator of [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model] and the corresponding target inclusion. The inverse uses its inverse on the same summand, so the two composites are identities. Naturality follows after restriction to each summand from naturality of the tensor associator. In particular, no factors are permuted and no additional Koszul sign occurs.

source.place: Definition 10.1: associativity constraint, written explicitly on intermediate-vertex summands.

proof.text: For $E\star P$, all terms in $\bigoplus_uE(u,t)\otimes P(s,u)$ vanish except $u=t$, and that term is $I\otimes P(s,t)$. For $P\star E$, all terms in $\bigoplus_uP(u,t)\otimes E(s,u)$ vanish except $u=s$, leaving $P(s,t)\otimes I$. Use the left and right tensor unitors of [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model] to obtain natural graph isomorphisms $E\star P\cong P$ and $P\star E\cong P$. Their inverses are the inverse tensor unitors followed by the respective coproduct inclusions. The zero-summand assertions use the empty-coproduct calculation in Step 2, so they hold even when $R$ is the zero ring.

source.place: Definition 10.1: diagonal unit and its two unit constraints.

proof.text: To check the pentagon for four graphs, restrict each composite to a summand indexed by a length-four path $s=x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4=t$. Step 3 leaves all three internal vertices fixed, so both composites have the same target summand. Their maps on its four tensor factors are precisely the two sides of the tensor pentagon in [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model]. Equality on all summands proves the graph pentagon. For the triangle, summands with a nondiagonal factor of $E$ are zero. On a surviving summand the two composites are precisely the tensor triangle on $P(u,t)\otimes I\otimes Q(s,u)$, hence agree. Thus the constructed constraints satisfy the monoidal axioms. For $S=\varnothing$ the graph category has one object and one morphism and every condition is vacuous; for a singleton $S$ these constraints are exactly those of $\mathbf V$.

source.place: Definition 10.1: direct coherence verification by summand inclusions; tensor coherence is part of the cited closed symmetric monoidal structure.

proof.text:
Fix $P$ and define $R_P(H)(s,u)=\prod_t[P(u,t),H(s,t)]$, with morphisms induced by postcomposition in each internal Hom. The closed structure of [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model] and the coproduct and product universal properties give natural bijections
$$\begin{aligned}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf G_S}(P\star Q,H)&\cong\prod_{s,t,u}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf V}(P(u,t)\otimes Q(s,u),H(s,t))\\&\cong\prod_{s,u,t}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf V}(Q(s,u),[P(u,t),H(s,t)])\\&\cong\prod_{s,u}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf V}(Q(s,u),\prod_t[P(u,t),H(s,t)])\\&=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf G_S}(Q,R_P(H)).\end{aligned}$$
Explicitly, restrict a graph map to each $u$-summand, curry it, and collect the resulting maps using the $t$-product. The inverse projects to each $t$, uncurries, and extends from the $u$-summands. They are inverse and natural because restriction/extension, projection/tupling, and currying/uncurrying are inverse natural operations. This proves $P\star-\dashv R_P$.

source.place: Definition 10.1, printed p. 1596: right adjoint of left matrix tensor; direct Hom-set calculation.

proof.text:
Fix $Q$ and define $L_Q(H)(u,t)=\prod_s[Q(s,u),H(s,t)]$, with the same postcomposition action. Now use the other tensor-Hom bijection of [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model] to obtain
$$\begin{aligned}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf G_S}(P\star Q,H)&\cong\prod_{s,t,u}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf V}(P(u,t)\otimes Q(s,u),H(s,t))\\&\cong\prod_{u,t,s}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf V}(P(u,t),[Q(s,u),H(s,t)])\\&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf G_S}(P,L_Q(H)).\end{aligned}$$
Here transpose by first interchanging the two tensor factors and then currying; for homogeneous elements that interchange is $p\otimes q\mapsto(-1)^{|p||q|}q\otimes p$. Collect over $s$ to define the forward map. The inverse projects to $s$, uncurries, interchanges back, and extends from the $u$-summands. The symmetry is its own inverse and all operations are natural, proving the second adjunction $-\star Q\dashv L_Q$. Both constructions remain valid for zero graphs and empty indexing sets. Together with Steps 3-5 this is the asserted biclosed monoidal structure.
